title: Exercise installed Git hook wrappers and branch-aware release delivery
objective: Add end-to-end coverage that installs every documented Git hook wrapper, exercises wrapper dispatch and branch-aware repository operations in disposable repositories, and completes the next computed revision release without introducing a duplicate repository-version source.

branch.name: WI-0032-hook-delivery-tests
branch.rationale: The installed-wrapper and branch/release exercise must be planned on main and processed on a dedicated context branch before a primary-branch revision release.

request.text: Generate a new .docs/work-items/* in order to test through the newly created webhooks. Ensure they are installed and go through branch operations followed by a new revision release. Commit the new work item. Implement the new work item and perform a release.

scope.name: installed-wrapper-exercise
scope.description: Install all 28 documented Git hook wrappers in disposable repositories and execute each installed wrapper through scripts/git_hooks.mjs dispatch.
scope.reason: The dispatcher implementation was tested through copied modules; this work item must exercise the actual installed hook files and installation output.

scope.name: branch-operation-exercise
scope.description: Exercise work-item start, task-processing branch enforcement, merge completion, post-merge reminder, primary-branch release checks, and no-remote behavior in disposable repositories.
scope.reason: Branch operations and release gates are part of the installed hook behavior and need an end-to-end regression boundary.

scope.name: revision-delivery
scope.description: Complete a new revision release using the existing package.json version source, computed impact, annotated primary tag, and remote push when configured.
scope.reason: The requested exercise ends with a real primary-branch revision delivery.

nonGoals.name: hook-policy-change
nonGoals.description: Do not change the intended dispatcher policy or add new enforcement semantics; add coverage for existing behavior.
nonGoals.reason: This work item verifies the newly installed wrappers rather than expanding Git policy.

nonGoals.name: duplicate-version-source
nonGoals.description: Do not add currentVersion, suggestedVersion, a release-version file, or any second tracked repository version source.
nonGoals.reason: Version impact is stored in versionSuggestion while the package and primary Git tag remain the release sources.

nonGoals.name: server-enforcement
nonGoals.description: Do not claim server-side hook enforcement, package publication, or deployment from local repository tests.
nonGoals.reason: The evidence boundary is local Git/client behavior.

items.name: installed-all-hook-coverage
items.description: The implementation must install and exercise every hook in scripts/git_hooks.mjs ALL_GIT_HOOKS through the actual .git/hooks wrapper files.
items.reason: The user explicitly requested testing through the newly created webhooks and ensuring they are installed.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The test installs 28 wrappers, confirms each is executable and dispatches its own hook name, and confirms repeated installation is byte-for-byte idempotent.
The test preserves unmanaged hook content and verifies wrapper argument and stdin forwarding through an installed hook file.

items.name: branch-and-release-operation-coverage
items.description: The validation must exercise work-item start, task-processing branch enforcement, merge/post-merge behavior, primary pre-push release checks, and local no-remote delivery behavior.
items.reason: Installed wrappers must work during the branch operations that precede a release, not only in isolated dispatcher calls.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Disposable repository tests prove task processing is blocked on the wrong branch and allowed on the declared context branch after work-item start.
Disposable repository tests prove post-merge reminders, primary-only release-tag checks, annotated-tag alignment, and no-remote local release evidence.

items.name: revision-release
items.description: After implementation, validation, and primary merge, perform the next computed revision release using package.json and an annotated SemVer tag without persisting a duplicate version value.
items.reason: The requested branch exercise must conclude with a new revision release.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The release task derives the next revision from the latest reachable annotated tag and WI-0032 versionSuggestion impact, updates only the existing package version source, and tags the primary tip.
WI-0032 task and work-item validation pass with zero invalid objects and no unresolved references before the release tag is pushed.

versionSuggestion.rationale: Adds end-to-end regression coverage and performs a backwards-compatible revision delivery without changing dispatcher policy.
versionSuggestion.disclaimer: This is an inferred recommendation; increase the impact if final changes add public behavior or broader compatibility effects.
